title: publish-release.sh hard-refuses to publish without an opum-cli-e2e qualification receipt for the exact SHA and tarballs (OPAG-379 ruling 3)
description: Binding record: opum-doc docs/adr/harden-fleet-ci-against-a-single-runner-outage-and-unqualified-publication.md at origin/main 9222079, Decision ruling 3: publish-release.sh HARD-REFUSES to publish without a qualification receipt from opum-cli-e2e, unless an explicit override is written to the record it reads. Warning-only mode was considered and rejected (lore 0.9.0 shipped over a recorded NOT QUALIFIED result). The 0.9.2 release (LCLI-577) follows this by hand. This task makes it mechanical. FILED ONLY, on the orchestrator's instruction (2026-09-24T05:34Z). Implementation timing is the orchestrator's call. Open design points to settle against the ADR before building: where the receipt lives and in what format (the script must READ it, not accept a relay), and which fields bind it (release commit SHA, Release run id, the per-tarball sha256 that publish-release.sh already verifies).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The receipt location and format are agreed with opum-cli-e2e and cited by path
publish-release.sh exits non-zero before any publish when no receipt matches the version, run id and every tarball sha256; proven with a mismatched receipt AND a matching one as two measurements
An explicit override written to the record lets it proceed and is echoed loudly; no env var or flag alone bypasses it
--dry-run reports the receipt verdict without publishing

implementationNotes: RECEIPT LOCATION AND FORMAT agreed with opum-cli-e2e, 2026-09-25 (by message; e2e owns the writer and will file its own task). LOCATION: receipts/<product>/<version>.json on opum-cli-e2e origin/main, read with gh api repos/opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e/contents/receipts/lore/<v>.json?ref=main. CONSTRAINTS: (a) opum-cli-e2e is PRIVATE, so a public-repo GITHUB_TOKEN cannot read it. The reader must treat 404/403 as NO RECEIPT -> REFUSE, never as a retry that eventually passes. (b) e2e's main is promote-on-sight, so a receipt appears minutes after its PR merges. FORMAT: {schemaVersion:1, kind:'opum.qualification-receipt.v1' (the reader refuses an unknown kind), product, version, commit (40-hex), releaseRunId, runAttempt, tarballs:{<filename>: sha256} (from the release-run artifacts), verdict, counts:{pass,fail,blocked}, blocked:[row names], harness:{commit:<40-hex e2e SHA>, baseline:'baselines/<dir>'}, pairedWith:{quest:{version,commit}}, qualifiedAt, override?:{by,reason,task,adr:'<path>@<commit>'}}. The reader keys ONLY on verdict==='QUALIFIED' (the harness summary line reads NOT QUALIFIED on every run because the scale row is unbound, e2e TASK-107), plus a match of version, releaseRunId and every tarball sha256. An override is honoured only from the file, and printed verbatim on use. BYTES: the gate is only meaningful if the digest-checked tgz is the exact file passed to npm publish, with no repack (quest's win32 CRLF lesson, QCLI-368); verify publish-release.sh does npm publish <exact tgz>. OPEN: e2e points out that the ADR's Consequences section names publish-release.sh's refusal as opum-agent-owned implementation. The orchestrator ranked LCLI-578 first for lore-cli at 01:33Z, but confirm the reader is in lore-cli's scope before building. e2e offered to commit one example receipt as a fixture first: ask for it.

SCOPE RULED (opum-agent, 2026-09-25): the receipt reader in publish-release.sh is lore-cli's to build; lore-cli is the sole mutation owner of that file. The ADR's 'opum-agent-owned' names ownership of the RULING, not the code. Sequence: after 0.9.3's release-critical items (LCLI-575 + LCLI-571), and 0.9.3 does not wait for it.

Fixture receipt from opum-cli-e2e, 2026-09-25: receipts/lore/0.9.2.json, contract in receipts/README.md, landing via opum-ai/opum-cli-e2e#246 (OPEN, head 28edae0b on feat/TASK-109-qualification-receipts; e2e will send the origin/main commit once promoted). Read back from that branch by this session: version 0.9.2, commit 71f2c1e4 (= v0.9.2 tag peel), runAttempt 1, verdict QUALIFIED, 7 tarballs, pairedWith quest 0.9.0 @ e8eeaf14. DEVIATION from the agreed format: harness.commitMeaning is added; harness.commit is the commit that LANDED the baseline, not the one that ran it, so the reader must NOT bind on harness.commit. Not re-resolved here, relayed only: that the 7 sha256s equal npm dist.integrity, and the 463/0/1 counts. Re-read from main before building the reader against it.
